Class GyroHeading

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.robotics.navigation.GyroHeading
All Implemented Interfaces:
DirectionFinder
public final class GyroHeading extends Object implements DirectionFinder
A DirectionFinder over a Gyroscope: a virtual thread of its own reads the gyroscope's angular velocity every SAMPLE_MILLIS and integrates it, so the direction keeps counting while the program waits on something else, such as an infrared round trip to an RCX. The direction is Cartesian, counter-clockwise positive like a drive's turns, while the gyroscope's rate is clockwise positive; it does not wrap at a full turn. Read it from any thread.

An uncorrected bias of one degree per second drifts the direction a degree every second, and a robot that holds a heading turns itself by the drift. So calibrate while the robot stands still, after start(): between startCalibration() and stopCalibration(), or for a fixed time with calibrate(int), the thread averages the rate instead of integrating it, and later reads subtract the average.

A BufferedGyroscope, such as the BMI088 with its FIFO, keeps sampling while the thread waits, and each read adds every sample buffered since the previous one, so a turn that ends while the program is busy loses nothing. Any other gyroscope is read once a visit, its rate times the time since the previous read: a read that comes late still counts the whole interval, but at the rate it reads then. If a buffered gyroscope delivers nothing for FALLBACK_PERIODS sample periods, its buffer is taken as not working and it is read the same way.

Juno's threads take turns at loop backedges and method entries, so the thread can take the processor in the middle of time-critical work on another thread. When a read must not interrupt such work, give the heading a gyroscope whose reads wait for it, for instance by synchronizing on the object the work holds. Create it once at startup; reading it allocates nothing.
